Although CO₂ makes up only a small percentage of air, it absorbs some of the long-wave thermal radiation emitted by Earth. Increased CO₂ traps more heat in the atmosphere, raising Earth’s temperature and causing climate changes that can harm ecosystems and agriculture.
Only gases that absorb long-wave thermal radiation emitted by Earth contribute to the greenhouse effect. Gases that do not absorb this radiation do not trap heat in this way.

The greenhouse effect is the warming of Earth’s surface and lower atmosphere when greenhouse gases absorb some long-wave radiation emitted by Earth, reducing the heat that escapes to space. Increased greenhouse warming can raise sea levels, cause flooding and damage agriculture and food production. In moderate regions, summers may become longer and hotter, while winters become shorter and warmer.
